Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Device Enrollment Management?

In this glossary, Device Enrollment Management refers to: The process of registering and configuring devices to ensure compliance with security policies before granting access to enterprise resources or networks.

How is Device Enrollment Management used in cybersecurity?

In cybersecurity communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Implement device enrollment management to ensure only registered, compliant devices can access cloud applications and corporate networks."

Why does Device Enrollment Management matter in cybersecurity?

Device Enrollment Management matters because it supports clear communication in Cloud contexts for SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as CISSP, CompTIA Security+, and CEH.

Who uses Device Enrollment Management?

Device Enrollment Management is mainly used by SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders.

What category does Device Enrollment Management belong to?

In this glossary, Device Enrollment Management is grouped under Cloud. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?
